text:
Man Utd transfer news: Brentford defender Nathan Collins emerges as January target - Paper Talk
Plus: Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50m to spend in January; Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January; Man Utd will prioritise a move for a striker in January; Xabi Alonso retains the faith of Chelsea’s owners and leadership team
Monday 23 November 2026 22:47, UK
The top stories and transfer rumours from Tuesday's newspapers...
MANCHESTER UNITED
Brentford defender Nathan Collins has emerged as a strong candidate for Man Utd ahead of Calvin Bassey, who is expected to sign a new contract with Fulham, and Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite, who is valued at over £70million - Daily Mail
Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50m to buy Man Utd out of trouble in the January transfer window - Daily Mail
Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January, even if one of them is a loan deal - Daily Mail
Man Utd want a left-back after failing to sign cover for Luke Shaw in the summer with Barcelona's Alejandro Balde and Man City's Rayan Ait-Nouri potential targets again - Daily Mail
Manchester United will prioritise a move for a striker in the January transfer window as Mauricio Pochettino looks to drag his team out of the relegation zone - The Times

PREMIER LEAGUE
Xabi Alonso retains the faith of Chelsea's owners and football leadership team, despite an underwhelming start to his reign as manager - The Telegraph
Tottenham Hotspur wonderkid Luca Williams-Barnett is on the brink of signing a new long-term contract with the club, which will disappoint Chelsea and Borussia Dortmund - The Telegraph
Arsenal have been handed an encouraging injury boost after David Raya was able to drive himself home following his shoulder scare against Newcastle - The Sun
SCOTTISH FOOTBALL
Representatives from Leeds United have been keeping tabs on Celtic forward Camilo Duran this season - The Herald
The Scottish Football Association has been advised to delay the vote on its radical young player reforms until the end of the season - Daily Record
EUROPEAN FOOTBALL
Bayern Munich have come under criticism from FIFA's players' union and leading figures in the game amid accusations that the club is attempting to slash Jamal Musiala's wages following his diagnosis with a 'neurological dysfunction' - Daily Mail
WORLD FOOTBALL
The Saudi Pro League is considering whether to raise its foreign player quota before next summer's transfer window, which could spark another international recruitment drive - The Times
FIFA
Gianni Infantino's World Cup sell-off plan could have led to the commercial rights to FIFA's tournaments being floated on stock exchanges - The Times
Gianni Infantino's £15bn World Cup sell-off plot risked FIFA surrendering almost half its commercial rights for nearly a century while enriching executives by tens of millions of pounds - The Telegraph
RUGBY UNION
Dave Rennie has received the unequivocal backing of New Zealand Rugby to lead the All Blacks into the World Cup, despite the team suffering five defeats in a calendar year for the first time since 1998 - The Times
The South Africa assistant coach Mzwandile Stick used Xhosa, his mother tongue, on Monday to avoid being misinterpreted but could yet follow Rassie Erasmus in facing disciplinary action after comments he made last week about the Ireland fly half Sam Prendergast - The Times
Nearly half of Twickenham's Allianz Stadium could be empty for the opening night of the Nations Championship finals weekend - The Times
